title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continuing from the previous page). X is a conformal sphere, X = P(V) with V a complex vector space of dimension 2. G = Aut_conf(X) includes the antiholomorphic maps, and G+ = PSL(V). H is a compact subgroup of G, H+ = H ∩ G+, and H~ is the preimage of H+ in SL(V). A positive definite H~-invariant hermitian form on V, normalised to total area 1, gives a spherical metric compatible with the conformal structure. The aim is a 'canonical' spherical metric determined by symmetry data, as a tool for the 'surgery' (cutting and gluing) of conformal surfaces. On the previous page, when the cone Herm^{++}(V)^{H+} is a single half-line, the metric is canonical and invariant under Norm_G(H+).

This page treats the degenerate case, where the invariant cone is larger than a half-line.
(1) This happens iff H+ fixes two distinct points z, z' of X. In modern terms: H~ is compact, so V is completely reducible under it. By Schur, the invariant form is unique up to scalar iff V is irreducible. Otherwise V = L ⊕ L', and z, z' are the two lines.
(2) Hence H+ lies in Stab(z,z') ≅ C^*, whose maximal compact subgroup is T ≅ U(1). If H+ ≠ {1}, then {z, z'} is the fixed-point set of any nontrivial element of H+, so it, and hence T, are uniquely determined by H+.
(3) For H+ ≠ {1}, the H+-invariant metrics coincide with the T-invariant ones (marked 'à vérifier'). Indeed, a non-scalar diagonalizable element of H~ has commutant the diagonal torus. The invariant forms are therefore diag(a, b) with a, b > 0, which is one essential parameter a/b after normalisation.
(4) These metrics correspond bijectively to the T-orbits in X* = X \ {z, z'}. T acts freely on X*, as w ↦ λw with |λ| = 1. The correspondence sends a metric to its equator: the great circle with poles z, z', which is a T-orbit, i.e. a circle |w| = r.
(5) Consequently, choosing an H+-orbit (equivalently, a point of X*, which determines its T-orbit) singles out one such metric.
(6) If H = H+ nothing more needs to be said. The case with orientation-reversing elements (anti-involutions, inversions, and the extension N of Z/2 by T) is treated on the next page.
errors: The bracketed claim that {z, z'} is uniquely determined requires H+ ≠ {1}. If H+ is trivial it fixes every point, and the invariant cone is the full 4-dimensional cone. Grothendieck handles this implicitly, since his next sentence starts 'Si H+ ≠ {1}' and the next page treats H+ = {1} separately.
The claim 'H+-invariant = T-invariant', marked 'à vérifier', is correct: the commutant of a non-scalar semisimple element of SL2 is the diagonal torus.
Minor: T ≅ U(1) acts on X* through w ↦ μ²w, so the action is free as an action of T viewed as a subgroup of PSL. This is consistent with the 'NB'.

ideas.what: A compact group of conformal automorphisms of the Riemann sphere has a unique invariant normalised spherical metric iff its lift to SL2 acts irreducibly. Otherwise it is contained in a circle subgroup U(1) fixing two points.
ideas.modern_name: Schur's lemma / complete reducibility for compact subgroups of SL(2,C); classification of compact subgroups of PSL(2,C)

ideas.what: Bijection between U(1)-invariant spherical metrics with poles z, z' and the U(1)-orbits (latitude circles) on X \ {z, z'}, via the equator.
ideas.modern_name: one-parameter family of round metrics in a fixed conformal class invariant under a rotation group (Möbius dilations along the axis)

ideas.what: Using symmetry data (a compact subgroup H, plus choice of an orbit or point when needed) to rigidify a canonical spherical metric on a conformal sphere, as a tool for conformal surgery.
ideas.modern_name: canonical metrics from symmetry; equivariant normalisation of spherical pieces in gluing constructions
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure (cf. circle packing / canonical metric constructions)
ideas.where_published: Possibly related to the 'surfaces conformes / cartes' themes of Esquisse d'un programme (1984), but this specific normalisation is not published there as far as I know.

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary and correct Möbius-geometry bookkeeping: invariant hermitian forms under compact subgroups of SL2 and the U(1)-invariant round metrics parametrised by latitude circles. It is a careful preparatory step for the conformal-surgery program, but contains nothing absent from the classical literature.
transcription_corrections: 'Herm^{**}(V)' should be 'Herm^{++}(V)' (cone of positive definite hermitian forms).
'On vérifie aisément que cela revient : dire que' should read 'que cela revient à dire que H+ fixe deux pts distincts z, z' de X'.
'T ≃ U' most likely denotes T ≅ U(1) (the unit circle group); the inserted phrase reads roughly 'càd un groupe [isom.] à' and is not certain.
'le grand cercle passant comme pôles z z'' should be 'le grand cercle ayant comme pôles z, z'' (the equator); a struck word beginning 'l'é...' (probably 'l'équateur') precedes it.
'L'relation est obtenue' is probably 'La relation est obtenue en associant'.
Last lines: the parenthetical is uncertain; it likely says that each H+-orbit (contained in a unique T-orbit) defines one and only one such metric, rather than 'une des uniques telles métriques'.
'Si H = H+, il n'y a rien à ajouter. Dans le [cas contraire]...' continues as 'Au contraire' on the next page.
